In this lesson you will learn about troubleshooting SCR trigger and power control circuits and you will troubleshoot faulted SCR trigger and power control circuits.
INTRODUCTIONM
Both circuits operate very similar, one uses DC voltage and the other uses AC voltage.
The SCR's operate the same in both circuits. To produce current flow, the SCR must be forward biased and must have a gate current.
Voltage measurements quickly determine if the circuit is operating normally.
An incorrect voltage measurement indicates that the circuit is faulted.
Let's begin the lesson on SCR CIRCUIT TROUBLESHOOTING EXPERIMENT............
LESSON MENU
What resistance range is used when checking an SCR?
The most common fault in an SCR circuit is a failed semiconductor component, the SCR.
DISCUSSION
The SCR may short or open, however the effect is the same - the voltage across the load will not be correct.
A shorted SCR is ON all the time. In the DC circuit, you will not be able to turn power OFF to the load.
In the AC circuit, there would not be any rectifying action or power control to the load.
An open SCR stops current flow. No voltage is developed across the load in either circuit.
However, be aware that any other component failures will cause the SCR to operate incorrectly.

The procedures to check an SCR CIRCUIT are simple..........
1. Determine the type of SCR circuit, trigger or power control.
2. Determine if the circuit has the correct applied voltage and gate input signals. Use a multimeter or oscilloscope.

5. If the SCR is good, isolate the fault to one of the circuit components......
